newsitem.title: CHINA: China criminal law adds provisions on stock crimes.
newsitem.headline: China criminal law adds provisions on stock crimes.

text.p: China's new criminal law has added provisions on securities crimes for the first time and will help check insider trading and price manipulation, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.
The law was revised last week by the National People's Congress, the parliament, and will come into effect on October 1 this year, the newspaper said.
Under the new provisions, people involved in securities crimes face a maximum five-year jail term, detention and fines, the newspaper said.
The crimes include unauthorised share or corporate bond issues, insider trading, creating or spreading false securities information and rigging prices, the newspaper said.
China revived its securities markets in the early 1990s. In recent years, securities violations have become a feature of economic crime in the the country.
Last year, Chinese investigators probed 61,099 economic crimes, helping to avert 6.78 billion yuan in economic losses, officials figures show. Comparative figures were not available.
